accuracy.evidence: Every number was recomputed: 40 × 6 = 24 tens = 240, 30 × 7 = 21 tens = 210, 60 × 5 = 30 tens = 300; the six sort cards give 9 × 0 = 0, 0 × 6 = 0, 1 × 9 = 9, 9 ÷ 1 = 9, 6 × 1 = 6, 7 ÷ 1 = 7; in each triple only one pair is a multiple of 10 (2 × 5, 5 × 2, 4 × 5) and the totals are 70, 90 and 60; dealing 24 tens into 6 bowls leaves 4 tens each (240 ÷ 6 = 40) and 35 tens into 7 leaves 5 tens (350 ÷ 7 = 50). Challenge answers checked (50 × 3 = 150, 480 ÷ 6 = 80, 4 × 7 × 5 = 140). Every parameterised item was checked at its range corners by gate_items. The scope matches the Year 4 statutory wording in the National Curriculum in England word for word.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in NCETM's Year 4 multiplication and division guidance and the DfE ready-to-progress materials: dropping the tens (tile 24 for 40 × 6, Ann, tag tens), adding too many zeros (tile 2400, Col, tag zeros), treating × 0 like + 0 (step 2 predict option 8, Dee, tag plus0), tacking a zero on for × 0 (Fin, tag tack), 9 ÷ 1 = 1 (card feedback, tag div1), adding three numbers instead of multiplying (Hal, tag addall, m7) and stopping after the easy pair (Ida, tag drop).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). Related labs do other jobs: flagtenten builds a hundred from ten tens, flagpvc reads digit values, flagcomm flips arrays for commutativity and the long-multiplication lab runs a written method. This lab is about mental strategies only: dragging rows of tens counters until the known fact appears as tens, sorting × 0 / × 1 / ÷ 1 cards, dragging one number card onto another so the multiple-of-10 pair is done first, and dealing tens counters into bowls round by round.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner drags rows of '10' counters and the header reads '6 rows × 4 tens = 24 tens' before any answer is offered, so 'ten times the known fact' is seen, not told. Sorting forces the × 0 versus × 1 decision card by card. Joining the wrong pair still gives the right total but is flagged as the hard way, showing that order does not change the product while the easy pair is quicker. Dealing one ten to each bowl per tap makes 24 tens ÷ 6 = 4 tens visible before choosing 40.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks 40 × 6 with '24' (dropping the tens) and '2400' tempting; the counters then show 24 tens. Step 2 asks 8 × 0 with '8' (thinking of + 0) tempting; the sort rejects it with the named reason. Step 3 asks whether order changes 2 × 7 × 5 with 'Yes' tempting; joining any pair shows the same 70. Step 4 asks 240 ÷ 6 with '4' tempting; the bowls hold 4 tens each, so 40.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor has its own tag and message: tens (forgot that 50 is 5 tens), zeros (only one number had a ten), one and plus1 (× 1 keeps the number), plus0 and tack (× 0 is not + 0 or × 10), tensd and zerosd for 480 ÷ 6, addall and drop for 4 × 7 × 5, div1 and zero1 for 8 ÷ 1. Lab feedback names the slip too: '24 counts the counters, but each counter is worth 10', '9 ÷ 1 ... that group gets all 9', 'Right answer, but the hard way'.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 0.0 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 7.1 (limit 9.5). Kid paragraphs use short sentences with one worked example each (24 tens = 240, 9 × 0 = 0, 2 × 5 = 10, 24 tens ÷ 6 = 4 tens); the adult text uses the precise curriculum terms (place value, known and derived facts, multiplying together three numbers).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one strategy that a lab step practises; the adult text gives the curriculum reference, the five tasks and the named mistakes; hints point to the fact to use first rather than restating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android) for every step at start, mid Show me and end: up to 8 rows of 10-counters fit (tall ratio 1.35), the drag dot has a 56 px hit box, the sort boxes were renamed '= 0' and 'Stays the same' after '= the number itself' clipped at 360 px, the three answer tiles are 50 px tall, seven bowls fit with readable '5 tens' labels, and the footer space now grows with the message so text never covers the counters.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completes with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Add a row / Take away a row, Answer n, Pick 9 × 0 then Put … in '= 0', Do 2 × 5 first, Give each bowl one ten, '<name> is right'), and the aria-label is rewritten after each action with the question, rows and tens, cards left, the chosen pair, or the tens left and in each bowl.
